# html.nesting — Content nested outside its parent's content model

- **Check ID:** `html.nesting`
- **Default severity:** `warning`; users can override it in `seaworthy.config.json`.
- **Needs:** `html`
- **Standards:** HTML Standard
- **Source module:** `packages/verify/src/checks/html.ts`
- **Prose page:** [`docs/checks/html.nesting.md`](../html.nesting.md) — embedded below verbatim; write it there, never here.

Content is nested outside its parent's content model: interactive content inside interactive content, block content inside `<p>`, or `<a>` inside `<a>`.

## Why it matters

The HTML parser accepts this source, but it does not keep it: browsers splice the markup apart and move content into elements the source never said. Links wrap blocks whose second link silently opens a new link in the middle; text written inside a paragraph continues outside it; two buttons or links share one click target. Styling, focus, and screen-reader behavior stop matching the markup, and agents that transcribe the source will describe a page the browser does not show.

## What it checks

Three rules from the [HTML Standard's](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/) content models, on markup the parser accepts but then rewrites:

- **Interactive inside interactive.** Elements whose content model forbids interactive content descendants — `<a>`, `<button>`, and `<label>` — with one of the interactive elements (`a` with `href`, `audio`/`video` with `controls`, `button`, `embed`, `iframe`, `img` with `usemap`, `input`, `label`, `select`, `textarea`) nested inside. The control a `<label>` labels is allowed: the element named by `for`, or the first labelable descendant when `for` is absent. A hidden input (`type="hidden"`) is not interactive. Elements in foreign namespaces (SVG, MathML) are out of scope.
- **Block inside `<p>`.** `<p>` takes only phrasing content, so the parser closes a paragraph before it. The rule reports the block element that starts where the implicitly closed `<p>` ends: `div`, `table`, `ul`, `ol`, `li`, `dl`, headings, `blockquote`, `form`, `pre`, `hr`, `address`, `article`, `aside`, `figure`, `fieldset`, `main`, `nav`, `section`, `summary`, `center`, `details`, `dialog`, `dir`, `dt`, `dd`, `figcaption`, `footer`, `header`, `hgroup`, `menu`, `p`, and others. A nested `<p>` counts too. Intervening phrasing content (`<em>`, `<span>`, text) does not change the report.
- **`<a>` inside `<a>`, and `<button>` inside `<button>`.** The parser ends the outer element exactly where the inner one starts and rebuilds a copy of it afterwards. The rule matches that splice point, so the report names the inner link or button even when block elements sit between them in the source.

Each finding points at the innermost offending element.

## How to fix

```html
<!-- before -->
<p>Opening paragraphs for sale items
<a href="/item">Buy the widget <div>Widget framing</div> <a href="/specs">full specs</a></a>

<!-- after -->
<p>Opening paragraphs for sale items.</p>
<a href="/item">Buy the widget</a>
<a href="/specs">Full specs</a>
```

Close each `<p>` before starting block content, or wrap the block content in a `<div>` outside the paragraph; for inline layout inside a paragraph use `<span>` with CSS. Keep links one level deep (or restructure so only the inner link exists); give buttons plain text and controls their own space. Inside a `<label>`, keep only the caption and its control; label other controls with `for="id"` and keep them outside.

## Options

None. Default severity: `warning`.
